one_month_reasoning: No scheduled earnings before Oct 31: full Q3 results should land ~Nov 9-10 (Q3-25 full results were Nov 10). But TeraWulf issued PRELIMINARY Q3-25 results on Oct 28 2025 alongside a deal announcement [23], so an in-window preliminary print or deal release is possible, and it cuts both ways. Possible but unconfirmed in-window events: CB-4 first-hall commencement (targeted late Sept; no release or 8-K yet as of Oct 2 [19][20]), launch of the ~$3.5B Justified leveraged-loan/HY financing ('expected to launch this year' [22]), finalization of Anthropic's IG credit support, and the Oct 28 FOMC. None is firmly dated, and silence on CB-4 so far is a mild negative. The stock fell ~13% in late September on insider-selling headlines and is ~50% off its June high, so momentum and reversal offset. I stay near neutral: lognormal median ~$14.80, monthly sigma ~27% (91%/3.5 plus a touch for the possible preliminary release), essentially unchanged from round 1.

bear.story: Anthropic's IG support slips or the ~$3.5B Justified financing prices wide, CB-4/CB-5 slip further, and AI-infrastructure multiples compress. The market moves to contracted-only value: $3.4 at 10.5% to $4.5 split-rate, 12m out, with little pipeline credit. A Fluidstack refresh-funding problem on the 56% of rent Google does not back would add pressure.

base.story: CB-4/CB-5 deliver by mid-2027 (438 MW live), Justified financed and on track for late 2027, Muskie project financing in 1H27 and maybe one lease. The stock trades between my split-rate DCF (~$6.8) and NAV at a 7.5-8% cap ($9.8-11.4), plus pipeline optionality the market prices more generously than I do.

bull.story: A 250-500 MW IG lease at Muskie or Lake Mariner, Anthropic support and financing close cleanly (Justified at 8.5%: +$0.55), and developers rerate to 6.5-7% caps (NAV at 7% is $13.3 before new leases). Back toward the June highs and the $30-36 July sell-side targets.

thesis_break_reason: The contracted leases alone are now worth $4.48 12m out at the split rates ($3.42 at a single 10.5%), after deducting the Muskie collateral, the Justified minority interest and the TCV-consistent rent shape. A sustained close below ~$5.75 would mean the market gives no credit to the pipeline (Muskie alone is ~$1.3/share probability-weighted) and prices contracted rent above my split rates. Most likely something fundamental broke: the Justified financing failed or came punitive, Anthropic's IG support fell through, a Fluidstack credit event beyond the Google backstop, a large CB-5 or Justified overrun (WULF bears power-delivery cost risk under the PSC-approved RESA), or a dilutive rescue raise. Lowered from $6.50 because the contracted-only value fell ~$0.7 on the site-level fixes.

reasoning: Round 4 rebuilds my DCF site by site (monthly, from Oct 1 2026) on the checked inventory and splits the discount rate. (1) Sites: Core42 60 MW, CB-3 42, CB-4 168, CB-5 168 (= 438 MW, $8.3B TCV incl. amendments) and Justified 401 MW ($19B/20 yrs) are contracted cash flows at TCV with phased commencement. CB-4 is assumed from Nov-26 because commencement is unconfirmed. Justified capex to go is now $4.06B (round 3 counted the $353M already spent). The Justified 6.8% minority put is deducted (-$0.21B). The Muskie cash collateral ($295M) and $50M deferred consideration are in net debt; the $90M contingent consideration and the collateral refund or forfeiture are in Muskie's probability-weighted value. Chesapeake's undisclosed price is deducted at a $150M judgment. BTC mining is credited only until CB-5 takes its power. Abernathy is the sale proceeds only. The lapsed Fluidstack option and the international pursuit are valued at zero. Pipeline (LM-EXP, Lake Hawkeye, Muskie, Chesapeake) is probability-weighted at $2.93M NPV per leased MW net of build capex and fees: +$1.28B, above round 3's generic $0.79B mainly because Muskie is now explicit. (2) Rates: Google-backstopped Fluidstack rent at 8.5%, anchored on WULF Compute's 8.7% effective secured cost against these leases and Hut 8's IG secured spread; unbacked Fluidstack 9.75%, Core42 9.5%, Anthropic 9.25% until IG support is final; everything uncontracted at 10.5%. Single-rate DCF $5.72 vs split $6.79 (12m). The split adds only ~$1.07 because Lake Mariner's in-term value is net of near-term capex discounted at the same rate, and post-term and terminal value stay at WACC. (3) Corrections found in the rebuild: round 3 escalated an $850M LM average (≈$9.3B in-term vs $8.3B TCV), and its NAV capped the deck's term-average NOI ($1.5B) instead of forward NOI ($1.28B). These two drive most of the drop: single DCF $6.57 -> $5.72, NAV $13.65 -> $9.76. GPU-life approach unchanged (6-yr base; unbacked share now 56%; Core42 refresh allowance added because it has no backstop); IREN corrected to 5 yrs per the fact-check. (4) Blend $7.82 (split DCF 45%, single 15%, NAV 40%) vs $10.40 in round 3 (supervisor-adjusted ~$10.25). Ladder: same 50/50 method (scenarios $5.5/$11.5/$25 at 30/45/25%, sigma 0.40; lognormal median $12.3, sigma 0.85). P(>= $14.91) 0.405 -> 0.377. Moved less than fair value because the market has persistently priced the pipeline and IG-backed rent more richly than my DCF. The 1-month ladder is unchanged: nothing new is scheduled in October and CB-4 is still unconfirmed. Research: 5 searches (CB-4 status, Morgantown price, Justified financing, WULF Compute note yield); no new primary facts changed.

discounting.basis: In-term rent backed by an IG credit (the Google-backstopped 44% of Fluidstack rent) at 8.5%. Anchors: WULF Compute's 7.75% notes (8.7% effective, BB), which are secured by these leases and the Google backstop and were priced before completion; and Hut 8's Baa2 secured project notes at T+165 (~6.9% on today's 5.24% 10-yr) plus ~150bp for an equity-like residual. Unrated counterparties, between 8.5% and WACC: unbacked Fluidstack 9.75% (thin balance sheet), Core42 9.5% (no backstop, $90M prepaid), Anthropic 9.25% (unrated; IG support 'expected', not final; WULF bears construction and power-cost risk), moving to 8.5% when support is final (+$0.55/share). Project capex is discounted at its contract's rate. Post-contract, pipeline, corporate and terminal flows at the 10.5% WACC. Values are 12m-forward per share (today: $5.00 single, $6.03 split). A search snippet shows the WULF Compute notes yielding ~6.44%; the date is unverified and the number is not used. If it holds, 8.5% is conservative.
